sn5.5:1.2: Regarded as the greates in psychic power ([an1.237:1.1]()), and, with Khemā, the ideal nun ([an2.131:1.2](), [an4.176:2.2]()). She taught other nuns ([thig13.5:27.3]()), and was devoted to the Buddha ([pli-tv-bu-vb-np5:1.1.1]()).
sn5.5:2.1: These verses are included in Uppalavaṇṇā’s at [thig11.1:7.1]().
sn5.5:6.4: Despite her dauntless rejection of Māra here, a story in the Vinaya says she was once raped by a Vedic student who was infatuated with her ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj1:10.5.1]()). The Buddha declared that one who does not consent is innocent. It seems hard to reconcile the two events, unless the Vinaya incident was when she was young and not yet accomplished. If that were the case, perhaps Māra is deliberately capitalizing on the past assault, assuming she will be traumatized by it.
